items.title: Loading screen shows 0% indefinitely
items.what: In the first screenshot the central logo is displayed above the text "Starting up · 0%" with a completely empty progress bar and the footer "A SHOEMONEY AI LABS GAME" on a black background.
items.why: Players see no visual feedback that the game is actually loading for several seconds; on mobile this immediately feels broken and increases perceived load time.
items.how: Hook the real Three.js asset loading progress (or a fake 0→100 ramp over 2–3 s) to both the numeric label and the length of the horizontal bar so it visibly fills from left to right.

items.title: Score and timer numbers lack contrast on warm HUD
items.what: Across multiple screenshots the yellow timer (30 → 27) sits on a dark translucent header bar; the yellow is only marginally brighter than the background glow and has no outline or drop-shadow.
items.why: On a phone in bright ambient light the timer is hard to read at a glance, which is critical information in a fast-paced fighting game.
items.how: Add a crisp 2 px black outline or a subtle dark outer glow to all score/timer digits in the top bar; test at 390 px width.

items.title: MOVE & JUMP / STRIKE labels are too small to read comfortably
items.what: In screenshots 2, 3, 9 and 10 the white instructional text inside the two bottom circular zones is set in a thin sans-serif at roughly 10–12 px effective size on a 390 px wide canvas.
items.why: Touch-first mobile players glance at the controls constantly; unreadable labels force them to memorize or ignore the tutorial layer, hurting onboarding.
items.how: Increase font size by 40 %, tighten tracking, and add a soft dark backing plate or thicker stroke so the labels remain legible even when the sticks are being dragged.

items.title: Fighters sit too low, wasting bottom third of portrait screen
items.what: In the wide fighting shots (especially screenshot 8 and 10) the feet of both characters are only ~15 % from the bottom edge while a large empty tatami area occupies the lower third of the viewport.
items.why: On a tall phone this pushes the action away from the thumbs and makes the fighters feel small; the composition feels bottom-heavy and less cinematic.
items.how: Raise the camera or the fighters’ root position by ~80–100 px so the belt line sits near the horizontal center of the screen while still leaving room for the bottom HUD.

items.title: Right stick highlight does not clearly show chosen direction
items.what: In screenshot 4 the right (TECHNIQUE) stick shows a small yellow dot and a faint ring, but the highlight is low-contrast and does not scale or brighten when the stick is actively dragged.
items.why: Players cannot instantly see which of the eight directions is registered, especially during fast combos; this breaks the direct visual link between thumb and on-screen result.
items.how: Scale the inner yellow dot 1.6× and increase its opacity/glow intensity while the stick is touched; add a matching colored arc on the outer ring that rotates to the chosen quadrant.
